title: The bee’s cell is a hexagonal prism capped by rhombic-dodecahedral facets

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The bee’s cell is a hexagonal prism capped by rhombic-dodecahedral facets

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The hive-bee’s cell is a hexagonal prism closed at one end by three rhombic facets of a rhombic dodecahedron meeting at about 109° 28′, the configuration that encloses a given volume with the least surface.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: hexagonal prism closed by three rhombic facets at 109^\circ 28' (\cos\theta = -1/3); minimal surface for given volume

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The bee’s cell, then, is this figure incompletely formed: it is a hexagonal prism with one open or unfinished end, and one trihedral apex of a rhombic dodecahedron.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates”; topic “The bee’s cell”. Scope: comb cells of the hive-bee

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: hexagonal prism closed by three rhombic facets at 109^\circ 28' (\cos\theta = -1/3); minimal surface for given volume

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch07-11: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.81

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The geometry and constrained surface-area comparison are explicit and testable with routine 3D measurement. Public specimen imagery can resolve the anatomical statement, while the minimal-surface calculation is directly reproducible.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct honeycomb cells, measure prism sidedness and basal facet angles, and compare surface area with alternative closures at matched volume.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Image collections may lack calibrated internal 3D views.

Real comb deformation can obscure ideal angles.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is a specific geometric description of one structure, the hive-bee cell, and open X-ray volumes of that structure exist. Prism geometry is already implicit in the hexagonal segmentations, and the diagnostic cap angle is measurable if the cell base was scanned. The foundation-comb caveat lowers adequacy without removing the possibility of a direct test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On three-dimensional reconstructions of hive-bee comb, measure the prism angles in plan and the angles of the three rhombs that close the cell. Prism angles near 120 degrees and a trihedral angle near 109.5 degrees would support the rhombic-dodecahedron description; a flat or differently angled base would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Much of the X-ray material was built on experimental foundations, which may alter the base relative to natural comb.

The released tables report cell size and tilt, so the rhombic-cap angle has to be measured from the volumes rather than read off a column.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.95

discriminating power: 0.8

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: If a hive-bee comb cell is a hexagonal prism closed by three rhombic facets of a rhombic dodecahedron, then in 3-D measurements of bee-built cell bases (not foundation-formed bases) the three basal facets must be planar rhombi meeting pairwise at dihedral angles close to 120 degrees, with each rhombus having obtuse angles close to 109 degrees 28 minutes (arccos(-1/3)) and acute angles close to 70 degrees 32 minutes.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: No analysis was run. The file inventories and README files of the two candidate Dryad datasets were examined via the Dryad API (datasets endpoint and /files listing) and the README of dryad.z8w9ghxmw was read. Neither contains 3-D geometry of bee-built cell bases: dryad.z8w9ghxmw (Peleg lab, 19.2 GB) holds X-ray microscopy of comb built on 3-D-printed plastic foundation frames, whose cell bases are the printed plastic, plus cell-size tables and cell tilt angles; dryad.r4xgxd2f3 (Yang 2022) holds cell orientation (in-plane rotation) angles and cell counts of natural combs in spreadsheets, with no basal geometry. MorphoSource and other scan repositories require a login. No other public micro-CT or 3-D scan of natural comb was located.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. From a public micro-CT or 3-D scan of natural (foundationless) worker comb, fit planes to the three basal facets of each measurable cell and compute the rhombus obtuse angle at the apex of the base. The claim is supported if the median apex angle over >= 20 cells lies within 109.47 +/- 3 degrees and the facet-plane fit residuals are small relative to wall thickness (planar facets), with the prismatic walls meeting at 120 +/- 5 degrees in cross-section.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Refuted if the median apex angle differs from 109.47 degrees by more than 6 degrees (e.g. if bases are rounded or formed of a single curved surface with no three-facet structure in the majority of cells), or if fewer than half of the cells show three identifiable planar basal facets. Results in between are 'mixed'. If no public 3-D data of bee-built cell bases can be obtained, the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable.

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Thompson's claim has two parts: a geometric description of the cell (hexagonal prism, three rhombic basal facets meeting at the tetrahedral angle 109 deg 28 min) and a minimal-surface rationale. Only the geometric description is tested here; the minimal-surface statement is a theorem about the rhombic dodecahedron (and is in fact not the true minimum, as Toth 1964 showed), not an empirical matter. The test requires 3-D geometry of bee-built cell bases. The two Dryad datasets listed were identified as the only public comb datasets found on Dryad, Zenodo and figshare on 2026-10-31; their README files were read to determine whether they contain basal-facet geometry before any data were downloaded.

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
Dryad file inventory for doi:10.5061/dryad.z8w9ghxmw on 2026-10-31: s_1_raw_xrm_data.zip (11.99 GB), processed_XRM_data.zip (6.88 GB), 3D_reconstruction_movies.zip (220 MB), 2D_images.zip (61 MB), cell_size_data.zip, angle_data.zip (cell tilt angles only), angle_raw_data.zip, figure data zips, README.md (file id 4176003). The README states the comb was built on 3-D-printed foundation frames of varying cell size, so the cell bases are not bee-built and cannot test the rhombic-cap geometry.

Dryad file inventory for doi:10.5061/dryad.r4xgxd2f3 on 2026-10-31: README_file.txt and five spreadsheets of cell orientation angles and cell numbers for Eastern and Western honey bee combs; no 3-D data.

The claim remains testable: a micro-CT of foundationless natural comb (or Toth-style measurements of the three basal rhombi) would resolve it with the pre-registered criteria above.
